step1_figure.circuit_type: Delta-Sigma Modulator (DSM) Sensing Circuit for Resistive Memory
step1_figure.description: Figure 17.21 depicts a simplified DSM sensing circuit for 1T1R resistive memory where the switched-capacitor feedback network is replaced by a 25 kΩ resistor. A clocked comparator with built-in offset (Fig. 17.16) senses the bitline voltage against VDD/2 and drives PMOS switch M3, which along with common-gate PMOS M4 injects compensating charge into the bitline to balance the memory cell current.

comparator_offset_voltage.description: Built-in input offset voltage of the clocked comparator created by sizing mismatch (13/1 vs 10/1) on the differential input transistors

equation.explanation: The comparator is intentionally designed with an input offset Vos so that the DSM feedback loop drives the bitline to VREF + Vos rather than exactly VREF, ensuring non-zero sense current through Rmbit.
equation.assumptions: Input transistor with gate In- is sized 13/1 while In+ is 10/1.

sky130_expected.calculation: Vos ≈ (Vgs - Vthn) * (1 - sqrt(W1/W2)) ≈ (0.5V - 0.42V) * (1 - sqrt(10/13)) = 0.08V * 0.123 ≈ 10 mV to 50 mV depending on bias current and dynamic latch regeneration; textbook design targets Vos ≈ 50 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Designed deliberately around 50 mV in textbook; process variations and 1.8V VDD shift Vos within 20 mV to 80 mV.

average_bitline_voltage.description: Average steady-state DC voltage maintained on the bitline by the DSM feedback loop

equation.explanation: Delta-sigma modulation regulates the average bitline voltage precisely to the comparator switching threshold VREF + Vos.
equation.assumptions: Sufficient loop gain and feedback capability to track cell discharge current.

sky130_expected.reasoning: VREF is biased at 500 mV, and the comparator built-in offset raises the average bitline voltage by ~50 mV.

cell_sense_current.description: Average current flowing through the resistive memory cell during sensing

equation.explanation: Because the bitline is held at VREF + Vos and the far end of Rmbit connects to VREF, the net voltage drop across Rmbit is Vos.
equation.assumptions: Access transistor on-resistance is negligible compared to Rmbit.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Vos = 50 mV and Rmbit = 200 kΩ: Imbit = 0.050 V / 200,000 Ω = 0.25 µA (250 nA).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by Vos / 200kΩ with Vos ranging from 20 mV to 80 mV.

bitline_voltage_ripple.description: Peak-to-peak variation of the bitline voltage during DSM cycling

equation.explanation: Every clock cycle where feedback is activated, current injects charge onto Cbit, creating a voltage step that settles as current drains through Rmbit.
equation.assumptions: Cbit = 500 fF, clock period T = 10 ns.

sky130_expected.calculation: Feedback current through R2=25k when M3 is on: (VDD - Vbit)/R2 ≈ (1.8V - 0.55V)/25k ≈ 50 µA. For pulse duration ~2.5 ns: delta_Q ≈ 125 fC. delta_Vbit = 125 fC / 500 fF ≈ 0.25 V (settles dynamically to ~50 - 100 mV).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Continuous discharge by Rmbit and low duty-cycle pulse injection keep bitline excursion below 200 mV.

bitstream_density.description: Ratio of clock cycles M in which the feedback current pulse is enabled to total clock cycles N (duty factor M/N)

equation.explanation: Charge balance over N cycles requires the average injected charge to equal the charge extracted by Rmbit.
equation.assumptions: Linear charge feedback; R2 = 25 kΩ, Rmbit = 200 kΩ.

sky130_expected.calculation: For Rmbit = 200 kΩ: M/N ≈ 25k / 200k = 0.125 (12.5%). Over 50 cycles (500 ns at 100 MHz), M ≈ 6 pulses (6/50 = 0.12).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Textbook simulates M=6 for 50 cycles at Rmbit=200k (page 501).

sensed_resistance.description: Calculated value of the memory cell resistance derived from the DSM digital output count M/N

equation.explanation: Digital output ratio N/M directly maps back to estimated Rmbit.

sky130_expected.calculation: For M = 6 and N = 50: Rmbit_calc = 25k * (50 / 6) = 208.3 kΩ (actual is 200 kΩ).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Quantization over 50 clock cycles gives discrete M values; M=6 yields 208 kΩ.

minimum_sense_resistance.description: Minimum detectable resistance before DSM saturates at continuous ones (M = N)

equation.explanation: When Rmbit equals the pull-up resistor (25 kΩ), feedback must be active 100% of the cycles (M = N).

sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly equal to pull-up feedback resistor R2 = 25 kΩ.

maximum_sense_resistance.description: Maximum finite detectable resistance resolvable with N clock cycles

equation.explanation: Corresponds to the minimum non-zero count M = 1 over N cycles.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Single pulse in 50 cycles gives 1.25 MΩ as derived on page 501.

average_supply_current.description: Average supply current drawn from VDD by the DSM sensing circuit during 100 MHz operation

equation.explanation: Total current pulled from VDD includes comparator dynamic switching current and feedback resistor current.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text states Fig 17.21 draws ~20 µA at 100 MHz. In SKY130 at VDD=1.8V, comparator dynamic power is higher, yielding 25 µA to 60 µA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Resistor feedback branches consume ~5 µA average while dynamic comparator clocks at 100 MHz.

step3_testbench.description: Transient simulation of the simpler DSM sensing circuit (Fig 17.21) with 100 MHz clocking over 600 ns (Baker CMOSedu methodology). Measures bitline DC average, ripple, comparator offset, bitstream pulse density M/N, estimated Rmbit, and average VDD current consumption.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Simpler DSM Sensing Circuit (Fig. 17.21)
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameter definitions for transistors
.param W_xm1=10u  L_xm1=1u
.param W_xm2=20u  L_xm2=1u
.param W_xm3=20u  L_xm3=1u
.param W_xm4=20u  L_xm4=1u
.param W_xm5=10u  L_xm5=1u
.param W_xm6=10u  L_xm6=1u
.param W_xm7=20u  L_xm7=1u
.param W_xm8=20u  L_xm8=1u
.param W_xm9=10u  L_xm9=1u
.param W_xm10=13u L_xm10=1u
.param W_xm11=10u L_xm11=1u
.param W_xm12=10u L_xm12=1u

* Power Supplies
VDD VDD 0 1.8
VREF VREF 0 500m

* 100 MHz Clock Source (Period 10ns, 50% duty cycle)
Vclock clock 0 pulse(0 1.8 0 100p 100p 4.9n 10n)

* DUT Netlist from Fig. 17.21
xm2 N003 N002 N001 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm4 vbit VREF N003 N003 sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
X_U1 vbit VREF N002 Out clock VDD 0 SUB_1
Cbit vbit 0 5e-13
R1 VREF vbit 200000.0
R2 VDD N001 25000.0

* Subcircuit definitions
.subckt SUB_1 inp inm q qi clock VDD GND
  xm1 N003 inp GND 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
  xm2 Outm Outp VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
  xm3 Outp Outm VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
  xm5 N002 Outm N004 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
  xm6 N001 Outp N003 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
  xm4 Outm clock VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
  xm7 Outp clock VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm7} l={L_xm7}
  xm8 Outm clock N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
  xm9 Outp clock N002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm9} l={L_xm9}
  xm10 N004 inm 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm10} l={L_xm10}
  X_U1 Outp q qi VDD 0 NAND_2
  X_U2 qi Outm q VDD 0 NAND_2
.ends SUB_1

.subckt NAND_2 A B Out VDD GND
  xm3 out B VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
  xm8 out A VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
  xm11 N001 B GND 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm11} l={L_xm11}
  xm12 out A N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm12} l={L_xm12}
.ends NAND_2

* Transient Analysis matching Baker's original simulation (600ns)
.tran 0.1n 600n 100n uic

.control
run

* 1. Average bitline voltage (Vbit_avg)
meas tran vbit_avg avg v(vbit) from=100n to=600n

* 2. Bitline voltage ripple (peak-to-peak swing)
meas tran vbit_max max v(vbit) from=100n to=600n
meas tran vbit_min min v(vbit) from=100n to=600n
let delta_vbit = vbit_max - vbit_min
print delta_vbit

* 3. Comparator offset voltage Vos
let v_os = vbit_avg - 0.500
print v_os

* 4. Cell sense current Imbit
let i_mbit = v_os / 200000.0
print i_mbit

* 5. Bitstream density M/N from average value of Out (Out is 1.8V when feedback active)
meas tran vout_avg avg v(Out) from=100n to=600n
let m_over_n = vout_avg / 1.8
print m_over_n

* 6. Sensed resistance Rmbit_calc
let rmbit_calc = 25000.0 / m_over_n
print rmbit_calc

* 7. Average supply current drawn from VDD
meas tran idd_avg avg i(VDD) from=100n to=600n
let idd_mag = -idd_avg
print idd_mag

quit
.endc
.end
